title: Pratik Kumar Chouhan vs State Of Odisha .... Opposite Parties on 14 July, 2025

paragraphs.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF ORISSA AT CUTTACK

 ABLAPL No.3614 of 2025

 Pratik Kumar Chouhan .... Petitioner
 Mr. A. Mohanty,Sr. Advocate


 -versus-

 1. State of Odisha .... Opposite Parties
 2. Rachana Mohanty

 Mr. S.N. Das, ASC
 Mr. L.K Maharana, Advocate
 (Informant)

 CORAM: JUSTICE V. NARASINGH
 ORDER

02. 1. Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and
 learned counsel for the State as well as the Informant.

2. The Petitioner is seeking pre-arrest bail in
 connection with G.R. Case No.248 of 2025 pending in
 the Court of learned S.D.J.M., Cuttack, arising out of
 Mahila P.S. Case No.49 of 2025 for commission of
 offence punishable under Sections 115(2)/296/85 of
 BNS and Section 4 of DP Act.

3. It is submitted by the learned senior counsel
 that taking into account the litigation, inter se,
 between the parties, the Petitioner may be protected
 by pre-arrest bail.

4. Such submission is opposed by the learned
counsel for the State as well as the Informant referring
to the memo of documents which are placed on record
including the Plaint in C.S No.477 of 2025, which
relates to the ownership of the Car between the
parties, which was filed by the Petitioner as plaintiff in
the Court Senior Civil Judge 1st Court, Cuttack in
which the Informant has already appeared and
application for divorce under Section 10 of the Indian
Divorce Act by the Informant in C.P Case No.51 of
2025, pending in the Court of Family Judge,
Bhubaneswar.

5. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the
Informant that just to wriggle out of the criminal
liability, the Civil Suit has been instituted and merely
because of the filing of the Civil Proceeding, which is
filed admittedly, after the registration of F.I.R, the
same not to weigh with this Court, in considering the
prayer of the Petitioner. And, taking into account the
nature of allegations, he ought not to be protected by
pre-arrest bail.

6. On considering the rival submission, it is
directed that on surrendering within three weeks hence
and moving for bail, the Petitioner shall be released on
bail by the learned Court in seisin on such terms as
deemed just and proper.

7. Before releasing the learned Court shall verify
 as to whether this order has been assailed before the
 Apex Court and if so, the result thereof.

8. It is needless to state that the Petitioner shall
 cooperate with the ongoing investigation.
9. Accordingly, the ABLAPL stands disposed of.

(V. NARASINGH)
 Judge
 Soumya
